history_review.result: Original summon implementation omitted the equipment eligibility check and OTHERSELF reply. Existing creation and World ID allocation are retained.
Preserve the learned-versus-innate level-zero distinction; do not copy unlearned basic-skill placeholders. Preserve the explicitly different tame/evocate policy pending reference evidence.
Recall-save arrival callback and existing lifetime/restoration behavior are unchanged.
Preserve paid cast authorization, authoritative power and equipment/ammunition checks. The new copied-skill filter reuses existing eligibility helpers.

current_change.integrity: Reply only for an active visible template-zero recall registered to the supplied owner. Reject guessed IDs, foreign ownership, other object types, stale/replaced/deleted/expired recalls, loading and secondary recipients. A locally present secondary owner copy may supply appearance. Only equipped items are serialized, sorted by slot, with the owner's item registration identity.

sql_player_exchanges.acceptance: The two complete post-exchange snapshots and pending direct item writes/deletes share one synchronously committed SQL queue record before either player's deferred success packets are published. Failed publication quarantines both sessions and excludes partial state from logout/item saves.
sql_player_exchanges.recovery: The existing single DB lane applies both native snapshots in queue order. A late failure or process death retains the entire record; startup/character admission waits for recovery. The native game-table writes themselves are sequential, not one cross-player SQL transaction.
sql_player_exchanges.session_lifecycle: Trade acceptance binds the original character ID/session key. Ask, accept, offer and confirm reject unavailable partners. Socket disconnect and teleport/map exit share teardown without transferring the old trade to a relogged player.

history_review.result: The original same-map staged-offer/capacity/confirmation logic did not checkpoint both character currencies/inventories together. Preserve snapshot copies, offer revalidation and both capacity guards; add SQL durability before success.
Keep the existing recipient block-list guard.
Keep tournament character restrictions, including rechecks on continuation.
Shared trade teardown preserves native teleport result/name ordering and existing pending-teleport/cast/state gates. The added entry point is socket disconnect.
